1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3.strategy: The natural developing move: the knight watches the centre and keeps every plan open, from a fianchetto to a central pawn break. White completes the symmetrical set-up and leaves Black to decide how sharp the game becomes.
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3.name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation, Three Knights Variation

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3.strategy: Prepares to bring the bishop to the long diagonal before the knight is committed, so White can wait and see what Black does in the centre. The game stays flexible and manoeuvring: sound and patient, with Black free to choose between a quick central strike and quiet development.
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3.name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation, Fianchetto Variation

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 Nc6.strategy: Develops the knight and adds a second guard of d4, so White cannot easily take the centre with a pawn. The structure stays symmetrical and flexible: a patient game of piece play in which both sides choose their moment to break in the centre.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5.strategy: Strikes at the centre at once and offers to trade the d-pawn for White's c-pawn. Black gets a knight on d5 and easy development; the price is that the symmetry is gone and White has a target to aim at.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 e5.strategy: Grabs space with pawns on c5 and e5 that control d4, but fixes the structure: no black pawn can easily challenge a knight on d5 again, so White can settle there and only a piece trade removes it. Playable, but committal.
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 e5.name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5.strategy: Strikes in the centre before White's bishop has even landed, and offers to trade the d-pawn for the c-pawn. Black gets a centralised knight and an easy game, while White aims the bishop and the c3-knight at that knight.
